clue.text: Unlucky criminal searched around empty house

indicators.note: around signals that one piece wraps round the other, the shell of house enclosing the reworked letters
an empty word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters of house
something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters of searched are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A burglar ransacks a deserted house and finds nothing worth stealing: bad luck for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' makes ARDCHEES; 'around' joins the pieces, though it is the house's shell that ends up outside. Hard cheese is British slang for tough luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British idiom for bad luck, often said with little sympathy, so it serves as an exclamation meaning unlucky.

clue.text: Faith invested in Telegraph operatives

indicators.note: something invested in a phrase is lodged inside it, so the letters sit within the words Telegraph operatives

explanation.surface: Trust is placed in the newspaper's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith and this word are synonyms in the sense of trust or confident expectation, as in faith, love and charity.

clue.text: Censure concerning degree of alcohol

parts.note: re is a short word for concerning or about, as in business letters
proof is the scale measuring the strength of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone is told off over how strong their drink was.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is a rebuke or formal criticism, which is exactly what a reproof is.

clue.text: Such theatrical demands caught everyone in the end

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here inside the word for the end

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end, as in it's curtains for him
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An audience demanding more catches every member of the cast as the show ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' meaning death or the end is informal; C and ALL go inside it before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: When an audience applauds for the cast to return to the stage, it is demanding bows in front of the drapes at the show's close.

clue.text: Ambassador's neglect during bad year

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other
something gone bad is spoilt, so the letters of year are rearranged

parts.note: to miss something is to neglect or overlook it

explanation.surface: A diplomat's failure to act over an awful twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' gives EARY, and 'during' splits it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission is an emissary, so an ambassador is an example of one.

clue.text: Balloons considerably on board ship

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the second piece is placed within the first

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
well can mean considerably, as in well over the limit

explanation.surface: Party balloons are loaded in great numbers onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships' names carry SS, 'steamship', which supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Balloons as a verb means expands or puffs up, a synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Capital equipment must need adjusting at the outset

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as for drilling or sailing

indicators.note: at the outset points to the very start of the word adjusting

explanation.surface: Money spent on kit will need tweaking from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money, but it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Letters inclined to favour the right

definitions.text: Letters inclined to favour the right

parts.words: Letters inclined to favour the right
parts.note: reads like correspondence from people leaning to the political right, but describes type that slants rightwards

explanation.surface: Letters to the editor showing a conservative bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping printed type leans towards the right of the page, which is the defining feature of this typeface style.

clue.text: Adversary who's not against revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of not against are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opponent turns out to be a rebel who doesn't oppose after all.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary is an opponent or foe, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cheeky one taken in by caller — a person who's not a real threat

definitions.text: a person who's not a real threat

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so these pieces sit within the caller

parts.note: a pager is a device that calls or bleeps someone
pert means cheeky or saucy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow is fooled by a phone caller, who turns out to be harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caller' looks like a person phoning, but it is the bleeping device.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone or something that looks fearsome but is actually powerless.

clue.text: Good deal, but hard work if starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: graft is British slang for hard work

explanation.surface: A job is a bargain, but only demands effort if you begin it late.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is idiomatically a large number, so it means a good deal.

clue.text: Temporary worker in stable gets limited accommodation

parts.note: a stand-in is a temporary substitute
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A temp at the stables ends up with only a cramped place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Space for people on their feet, as at a concert or on a train, is room of a restricted kind.

clue.text: Garment worn by strong man regularly?

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of strong man is taken

explanation.surface: Is this robe habitually worn by a muscleman?
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman citizen's loose outer robe is a garment.

clue.text: Divulging secrets, and leaving

definitions.meaning: to split on someone is to inform or tell tales
to split is slang for to depart

explanation.surface: An informer blabs and then makes a quick exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal uses of split: to betray secrets and to go away.

clue.text: Fear parts of canal system may give such a shock

parts.note: dread means fear
locks are the gated chambers that raise and lower boats on a canal

explanation.surface: Terrifying parts of the waterways might frighten anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright, but here it is a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a bushy mass of hair, and matted ropes of hair are one style of it.

clue.text: Best dress given to engineers for industrial plant

indicators.note: given to means the second piece is attached after the engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
finery is one's best clothes

explanation.surface: The sappers are handed their smartest outfits to tour a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where crude oil or sugar is purified is a works of this kind.

clue.text: Complete agreement sees son in marriage

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a union is a marriage
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wedding at which the son is happily in total accord.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in full accord is an idiom drawn from voices singing the same note.

clue.text: Newspapers should cover hospital department awards

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping round it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: The papers ought to report on prizes won by a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, awards means bestows or hands over formally, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Statistician — or a knowledgeable boxing type who's socially inept

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A clever number-cruncher, or a boxing expert, who lacks social graces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' seems to be the sport but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, after the dull waterproof jacket such people supposedly wear.

clue.text: Private log — a terrible mistake

parts.note: own means private or personal, as in one's own room

indicators.note: terrible signals a mess, so the letters of log a are reordered

explanation.surface: A secret diary records an awful blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, it is scoring into your own net; figuratively, any self-inflicted error.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-defeating blunder is the figurative sense of this football term.

clue.text: Coaches wear them out!

definitions.meaning: sports shoes are worn outdoors, and these coaches also exhaust their athletes

explanation.surface: Coaches exhaust the athletes they train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear them out' sounds like exhausting someone but means wearing shoes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people who coach and sports shoes one wears.

clue.text: Former lovers must accept rent that's rising comes to an end

indicators.note: accept means take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: exes are former partners

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word for rent goes backwards

parts.note: a rip is a rent or tear

explanation.surface: Ex-partners face rising rent as their tenancy runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is a tear; 'rising' reads it upwards, giving PIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is to end or run out, as a lease or licence does.

clue.text: Scholar can expect to be keeping secret

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the words enclose the answer

explanation.surface: An academic can expect to be sworn to confidentiality.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious or understood only by a few, a synonym of secret.

clue.text: Letters left with house in Westminster

parts.note: and means with or plus
the House of Lords is one chamber of the UK Parliament at Westminster

explanation.surface: Correspondence left behind at Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like mail but means people who let property.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rent out property are those who let it, so they are lessors or letters.

clue.text: Good copy, but yawn!

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A decent piece of journalism, but a boring one.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawn as a verb can mean open wide, which is the sense of the answer as a wide opening of the mouth.

clue.text: Kid won't finish these drinks

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is cut

parts.note: to kid is to tease or joke with

explanation.surface: A child refuses to finish these beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child but is a verb meaning to rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups of the beverage brewed from leaves are drinks.

clue.text: Criminal has no right to fiddle

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker has no right to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books is to falsify accounts, so cook means fiddle in the sense of fraud.

clue.text: Dish for passengers at sea?

definitions.meaning: the principal plate of a meal
main is an old word for the open sea, and a ship's course across it is followed by its passengers

explanation.surface: What dish is served to people on a cruise?
explanation.definitionFit: The chief dish of a meal and, punningly, the route taken across the ocean.

clue.text: Only the French like this to have precedence

indicators.note: having precedence means coming first, so the words for like this lead

parts.note: so means thus or like this
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Only the French would insist that this should take priority.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, as in the sole survivor.

clue.text: Films by spies worried prophets of doom

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are set next to each other
worried means agitated, so the letters of spies are jumbled

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as is a mist on glass

explanation.surface: Movies made by anxious secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' looks like movies but means thin coatings; 'worried' rearranges SPIES to PESSI.
explanation.definitionFit: People who always expect the worst outcome are gloomy forecasters.
